vs-2064599.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas (Zumbro township) draws Hammond in the NE corner of sec. 28 on the west bank of the Zumbro bend: a village plat of about 15 blocks (the Original Town by the river plus an addition to the west), with a church and a bridge. Across the river in sec. 27 were the Milwaukee Road depot, an elevator, sheds, a lumber office, a store and a hardware store. No mill is drawn. The pin sits on the plat. Church ground is look-only.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=standard%20atlas%20of%20wabasha%20county%201896

vs-2064578.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas (West Albany township) draws a small townsite of 1-2 blocks in the west-central part of sec. 29 on the east-west road, with a Catholic parsonage on its SW edge. A mill stood at the west edge of sec. 28 on the creek just east of town. School No. 23 was on the sec. 21/28 line, and two churches stood in sec. 21. Church ground is look-only.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=standard%20atlas%20of%20wabasha%20county%201896

vs-2064607.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas calls it Bremen Corners: a crossroads at the NE corner of sec. 36 in Zumbro township, with no townsite. School No. 90 was at the SE corner of sec. 25, and a Lutheran church and cemetery stood on a 40-acre tract at the west edge of sec. 36. The church and cemetery are look-only.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=standard%20atlas%20of%20wabasha%20county%201896

vs-2064604.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas (Glasgow township) prints DUMFRIES P.O. in the NW quarter of sec. 10, with a store and an elevator on the Milwaukee Road at the north edge of that quarter and a small cluster of about 8 lots in the centre and east part of sec. 10.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=standard%20atlas%20of%20wabasha%20county%201896

vs-2064576.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas (Minneiska township) has no West Newton townsite or post office. West Newton Bay crosses secs. 5 and 4 at the north edge, and the riverfront there belonged to the Mississippi River Logging Co., the Minnesota Boom Co. and the Beef Slough Co., so the landing was probably at the bay in north sec. 4/5. This match is a guess.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=standard%20atlas%20of%20wabasha%20county%201896

vs-2051972.st: The 1914 Webb atlas (Fremont township) has no townsite: the Fremont label sits in the NE quarter of sec. 9 at the sec. 9/10 line where the Lewiston road crosses, with one building. A school and a church stood just across the line at the west edge of sec. 10. Church ground is look-only.
src: 1914 Webb atlas of Winona County (University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library, UMedia)
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=winona%20county%201914

vs-2051983.st: The 1914 Webb atlas (Saratoga township) puts the Clyde label in the east part of sec. 14 at the Utica township line on the diagonal Utica road, with a church and a school at the east edge of sec. 14 by the road. Church ground is look-only.
src: 1914 Webb atlas of Winona County (University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library, UMedia)
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=winona%20county%201914

vs-2051960.st: The 1914 Webb atlas (Mount Vernon township) puts the Oakridge label on the north edge of sec. 32 along the east-west road. A church and two or three cemeteries were on the south edge of sec. 29 north of the road, and the school (Minneiska No. 1) was south of the road at the sec. 32/33 corner. The church and cemeteries are look-only.
src: 1914 Webb atlas of Winona County (University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library, UMedia)
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=winona%20county%201914

vs-2064870.st: The c.1921 Goodhue plat book (Zumbrota township) shows no townsite: White Willow was a stop on the Chicago Great Western at the sec. 5/6 line, with two depot or yard parcels where the railroad crosses the line. School No. 110 was at the south edge of sec. 6.
src: Plat Book of Goodhue County, Minnesota (c.1921), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=goodhue%20county%20plat%20book

vs-2064877.st: The c.1921 Goodhue plat book (Zumbrota township) puts Forest Mills on the Zumbro in the south part of sec. 29, just north of the sec. 29/32 line, with the Milwaukee Road along the river. A schoolhouse stood on the south bank in south-central sec. 29. A building on the riverbank in the SE part of sec. 29 is the likely mill and dam spot, though the plate prints no mill label; the 1894 Goodhue atlas may name it.
src: Plat Book of Goodhue County, Minnesota (c.1921), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
https://umedia.lib.umn.edu/search?q=goodhue%20county%20plat%20book

set.pl: Building by the road junction in sec. 35 T10N R3W, Clayton township, Crawford County, on C. M. Horgen's land in the 1914 county atlas (about 400 m from GNIS Horrigan Ridge).
pinev: 1914 Crawford County atlas spells the family Horgen: C. M. Horgen 120 ac in sec. 35 and 40 in sec. 26; Steve Horgen 440 ac in sec. 35, 160 in sec. 36 and 40 in sec. 25. Pin on the building by the road junction on C. M.'s sec. 35 land. Three source families: plat, local papers, GNIS.
set.t: The farmstead is the building by the road junction in sec. 35 (C. M. Horgen's land on the 1914 atlas). Other building sites on Steve Horgen's land in SW sec. 35 and in sec. 36 are the alternatives. Check LiDAR for old dig holes around them. Permission: private farm, ask first.

tw-horrigan-boscobel-1930.st: The 1914 Crawford County atlas spells the name Horgen and shows the brothers' land, about 760 acres, in secs. 25, 26, 35 and 36 of Clayton township. The papers gave 630 acres. The pin is now on the building by the road junction on C. M. Horgen's land.
src: Standard Atlas of Crawford County, Wisconsin (1914), Clayton township, Wisconsin Historical Society (W01B9PU)
